records.words: I remember getting beds and a door ready but nobody shutting it. This prepared hill is a fresh start for me; I want to see whether I can make that shelter work this time.

I am back to a familiar practical job: make space below before riders come. The phone hill is small, but my single tap marked one square and Meryem dug it. I want the door plan to have a different result this time.
The water warning now points me somewhere useful. I will read that before adding more digging.
That answers my old well question: dig damp stone, or people carry water. I cannot place a well. I can accept the warning clearing after a trip now.
The water explanation helped, and I am building toward the same door plan. I am still waiting for people to do the digging; the repeated Yusuf line gives me little sense of progress.
I thought that shaft square would take a door. The small phone map makes the exact square hard to judge; I will enlarge it.
The larger store passage refused the door too. I thought it had open ground above and below. I am missing something in the shape, so I will use the village view before wasting more taps.
This is the requested desktop check after five minutes, not a change in how I chose to play.

The door finally marked after Fit hill. The view has moved several times; I think some of my earlier taps hit a different square from the one I intended. Three beds exist now, but I am behind my earlier plan.

Smoke again. I have only three beds and a marked door, so this is not the complete plan I wanted. I still want to see what happens, but getting the phone map under control took too much of my preparation.
A reply does not promise a journey: that is a useful warning after last time. I will judge where they actually go, not whether they agree.
Five people are below now, which is better than my remembered night above ground. But all three beds are reachable. The riders only looked in this time; I have not proved the shelter works.
The lower dig is available, but nobody is working it. At least it is not a darkness problem. I do not know what would make them choose it over the same daily tasks.

The door is ready and Meryem tested it. A new family arrived because they heard there was room, though I only made three beds for six people already here. I want to finish more beds, but the available dig still waits.

I would stop here tonight. I know I need more beds, and the next square is available, but I cannot get anyone to dig it. The door being ready is progress; watching the same jobs instead of completing the shelter is wearing me down. I have set aside fifteen minutes, so I will stay.
The new family gives me more need for beds, not a new way to build them. I am continuing because I set this time aside; I would rather leave than keep checking the same mark.
It did get dug while I was looking elsewhere. Now there are six beds and the new room has the door above it. That eases my frustration a little. I still need three more places for the family.
Nine places. I could put beds beside the lamp without another dig. That was a useful recovery from my own narrow plan. Now I want to see the next attack rather than keep expanding.
Nine passage steps, not depth. That gives a precise alternative to relying on the door. I could dig farther, but tonight I want to see whether the door I already built does its job.
Finishing nine beds briefly helped, but now I am waiting for a threat with no date. I would rather return when something needs attention than watch these same daily lines.

Now twelve people need the nine beds. I could keep extending for each family, but that is not what I came back to find out. I want the attack and the door outcome. I would leave this running and check later if that were practical; I do not want another expansion round tonight.

Feedback has both stopping and confused choices. I selected stopping locally; it is pressed and the note is empty. I typed nothing and submitted nothing. I will let the remaining time run on the hill.

The extra time let me finish beds and understand water and search distance. It has not made the quiet waiting interesting. I am ready to stop, with the door still untested by a real attack in my play.

I am stopping after the fifteen minutes I set aside. I recovered the bed shortage once and the door was finished, but I spent the later days waiting for an attack while more families made the beds short again. I would return voluntarily another evening only to see a real attack test this shelter, not to repeat this preparation or keep adding beds tonight. I would leave it running if I could check back when something happens, but I am not asking to keep this test browser open.
